## Project loop

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    I["Infrastructure<br/>Keir"] --> D["Model development<br/>Enoch"]
    D --> A["Model analysis<br/>Samuel"]
    A --> N["Agree next step"]
    N --> I
```

Each round should hand off documented inputs, evidence, limitations, and a next-step recommendation.

## Progress by stage

| Stage | Current evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure | Python pipeline downloads Yahoo `GC=F` futures data, builds forward realized-variance labels, and saves raw/prepared CSVs. An interactive notebook and focused tests support inspection. | In progress |
| Model development | Enoch added the data-preparation checklist and return-only candidate forecasts (expanding/rolling variance, EWMA, AR/MA of squared returns, ARCH, and GARCH). | Baselines available; evaluation pending |
| Model analysis | No out-of-sample comparison or model-selection decision is recorded yet. | Awaiting evaluation evidence |

## Data readiness

- The current working default is Yahoo Finance **`GC=F`**, a COMEX gold futures continuous series—not spot or a single fixed-expiry contract. The team may revisit the instrument.
- Yahoo Finance `XAUUSD=X` returned no data in the check recorded on 2026-11-06; `GC=F` was verified to return daily observations.
- Running the CLI or notebook downloads raw prices from Yahoo and writes raw and prepared CSVs under the Git-ignored `data/` directory.
- No downloaded raw market-data file is recorded in Git. Any Bloomberg export should remain local unless its license permits sharing.
- The prototype defaults to a five-observation forward realized-variance label; the horizon and target definition should be confirmed by the team before results are treated as project decisions.

## Git submissions by team member

The table and commit list below are generated from `git log --all` when this deck is rendered. They include all three team members, counting commits attributed to the author identities mapped below across locally available branches. They do not count uncommitted changes or independently enumerate GitHub PRs. Fetch branches first so recent teammate submissions appear.

```{python}
import subprocess

team_aliases = {
    "Keir": {"0keirli0", "keir"},
    "Enoch": {"enoch1uo", "enoch"},
    "Samuel": {"samuel"},
}

result = subprocess.run(
    [
        "git",
        "log",
        "--all",
        "--date=short",
        "--format=%h%x09%an%x09%ad%x09%s",
    ],
    check=True,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)

commits = []
for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
    commit_hash, author, commit_date, subject = line.split("\t", maxsplit=3)
    normalized_author = author.strip().casefold()
    member = next(
        (
            name
            for name, aliases in team_aliases.items()
            if normalized_author in aliases
        ),
        author,
    )
    commits.append(
        {
            "Member / author": member,
            "Commit": commit_hash,
            "Date": commit_date,
            "Submission": subject,
        }
    )

if not commits:
    print("No commits are visible in the current repository refs.")
else:
    counts = {member: 0 for member in team_aliases}
    latest = {member: "—" for member in team_aliases}
    for commit in commits:
        member = commit["Member / author"]
        if member in counts:
            counts[member] += 1
            if latest[member] == "—":
                latest[member] = f'{commit["Date"]} ({commit["Commit"]})'

    print("| Member | Visible commits | Latest visible commit |")
    print("|---|---:|---|")
    for member in team_aliases:
        print(f"| {member} | {counts[member]} | {latest[member]} |")

    print("\nRecent submissions visible in Git history:")
    print("| Author | Commit | Date | Submission |")
    print("|---|---|---|---|")
    for commit in commits[:12]:
        subject = commit["Submission"].replace("|", "\\|")
        print(
            f'| {commit["Member / author"]} | {commit["Commit"]} '
            f'| {commit["Date"]} | {subject} |'
        )
```

Before rendering, fetch shared branches so the report includes their latest commits:

```bash
git fetch --all
quarto render presentations/project-progress.qmd
```
